title: Use the slope formula
text: Since $$x=r cos\left(\theta\right)$$ and $$y=r sin\left(\theta\right)$$, the slope is $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{r'\sin\theta+r\cos\theta}{r'\cos\theta-r\sin\theta}$$

title: Plug in
text: At $$\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$$, $$r=2$$ and $$r'=-4sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=-2\sqrt{3}$$. Then $$r' sin\left(\theta\right)+r cos\left(\theta\right)=-3+1=-2$$ and $$r' cos\left(\theta\right)-r sin\left(\theta\right)=-\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}=-2\sqrt{3}$$, so the slope is $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$.
